reader.q: Is this about my situation now? It passes if it refers to what is happening or coming next. It fails only if it is about something already over — stale news.
reader.kill: it is about something already over — stale news. Referring to what is happening or coming next is not a failure.

reader.q: Does it need me now, or can it wait? Is there a clock on it?

Is there something here I had not already worked out? The line may mention what I know. It passes if it adds one thing I have not computed — a deadline, a consequence, a number that follows from my situation. It fails only if everything in it is already known to me.
reader.kill: everything in it is already known to me. Mentioning what I know is not a failure when the line also adds one thing I have not computed.

reader.q: Does it name a pain I have actually been through?
reader.kill: In the words I would use, not the seller's.

reader.q: Is there an upside, or only a warning?
Does this land on me, or on someone else in my organisation?
reader.kill: Not my decision, not my read.

seller.q: Which of our capabilities touches what she is dealing with now, or will be within a quarter?
Which of HER goals does that capability move? Not the company's — hers.
Where do we have evidence? A comparable situation we have handled.
What is the job she would hire us for? State it as her progress, never as our product.
Of the candidates that survive, which one scores highest against the reader's trace?
